title: Thane Heins coil reverses generator drag, replicated by Gary

tellings.quote: when I put his coil on, which has higher inductance, when you tell that coil to power a load, the rotation speed increases and the input current goes down.

plain: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he repeated a test based on the work of an inventor in Canada named Thane Heins. McKinnon says that when he fitted Heins's special coil, a coil of wire with higher inductance, and asked it to power something, the generator spun faster while the electricity going in went down. If true, it would go against the normal rule that a generator slows down when it has to do more work.
